content.text:
This is amoxapine's N-methyl analogue, loxapine: 2-chloro-11-(4-methylpiperazin-1-yl)dibenzo[b,f][1,4]oxazepine.

Reading the drawing region by region:
- **Piperazine:** an N-methylpiperazine, with H3C on the left nitrogen. Its right nitrogen is bonded to C11.
- **Central ring:** C11 is double-bonded to the ring N (the imine). That N attaches to the right benzene ring. The right benzene ring is bonded through O to the lower-left benzene ring, which in turn bonds back to C11.
- **Chlorine:** it sits on the lower-left benzene ring, para to the oxygen-bearing carbon. In the drawing, the ring carbon attached to C11 is at the top (815,770), the carbon attached to O is at the upper right (903,818), and Cl is on the far-left carbon (728,918). Going around the ring from C11: C(ipso, 815,770), then C(728,818), then C-Cl (728,918), then C(817,968), then C(903,918), then C-O (903,818).

Writing the SMILES:
CN1CCN(CC1)C1=Nc2ccccc2Oc2ccc(Cl)cc12

Checking the ring closure: C1(=N) is C11, and N is bonded to c2ccccc2, where the last aromatic carbon bears O. Then O connects to c2, the carbon attached to O, followed by c (the carbon at 903,918), c (817,968), c(Cl), c (728,818) and c12 (the ipso carbon bonded to C11). The Cl carbon is therefore meta to the ipso carbon and para to the O-bearing carbon, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: CN1CCN(CC1)C1=Nc2ccccc2Oc2ccc(Cl)cc12
